subject: Proposal to consolidate feature-flag vendors to capture savings and simplify ops
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 29 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Consolidation ask — evaluate single FF vendor vs dual vendors

Team —

We have two parallel renewals coming up: our LaunchDarkly subscription for core feature flags and an Optimizely contract for experimentation and flagging in a handful of products. Up front: I want a concise recommendation on whether we should consolidate to a single vendor (and which) vs keep the current split.

Please review the attached cost model (FF_consolidation_cost_model.xlsx) and provide:
- High-level 12-month TCO delta (licensing + expected engineering migration cost + professional services)
- Risk summary (integration complexity, SDK changes, data export/import needs)
- Key negotiation levers and estimated achievable discount ranges
- Recommended next step (negotiate with LD, opt to renew both, or run a consolidated RFP)

Target: get recommendation and rough numbers by Monday EOD (Aug 2). I’m triaging this because finance wants our input ahead of the renewal windows.

Thanks —
Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
VP, Platform & Product Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 30 Jul 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Consolidation ask — evaluate single FF vendor vs dual vendors

Evelyn / team —

Quick numbers from infra side after a 2-hour audit:
- Current annual vendor spend (approx): LaunchDarkly $210k, Optimizely $135k = $345k
- Migration engineering effort estimate to consolidate onto a single platform: 2.5 - 4.0 engineer-months (depends on test harness & rollout states) -> ~$85k - $140k in direct labour cost basis
- Ops/Runbook work: small, ~0.3 EMs ongoing; not a major recurring delta

If LD offers an enterprise consolidation discount of 20-30% for combined usage, break-even on first year is likely (license savings cover migration). If discounts are minimal (<10%), consolidation still reduces complexity but the first-year cost could be neutral to slightly negative.

I attached a short export of our flag footprint and approximate call volumes. Also noting: Optimizely hosts some experimentation logic we’d need to port (feature gating + experiment SDK hooks) — migration will require a short QA push.

- Karthik
Principal SRE, Serving Runtime
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 30 Jul 2027 11:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Consolidation ask — evaluate single FF vendor vs dual vendors

Evelyn —

Commercial context from vendor side: we have good leverage with LaunchDarkly (long-standing relationship, usage growth). Amy Chen (LD AM) is responsive and typically flexible on multi-year/commit discounts and professional services credits. Optimizely is more status-quo focused; Nate (their rep) will push for value in experimentation suite pricing but historically harder to move on aggressive discounts.

Suggested negotiation playbook:
1) Start with LaunchDarkly with a consolidation ask + multi-year commit (18–24 months) — ask for technical migration credits for professional services and a minimum of 20% off list.
2) Put Optimizely on notice: request counter-proposal but make clear we prefer a single-provider solution if price + migration risk align.
3) Pause any immediate renew approvals until we have written proposals from both.

If we need Legal/Finance to expedite, I can surface this to my contacts and coordinate timing with procurement.

-Marissa
Head of GTM Strategy
From: Amy Chen <amy@launchdarkly.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 02 Aug 2027 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: LD renewal / consolidation quote and options

Hi Evelyn / Markus —

Thanks for reaching out and for the detailed context. Attached is a preliminary quote and two commercial scenarios:
- Scenario A (consolidation + 18-month commit): 28% discount off list + $35k in PS credits to help with migration & experience parity work. [Attachment: LD_renewal_quote_2027-08.pdf (PDF, 120KB)]
- Scenario B (renew both, standard renewals): 12% discount on existing seats, no PS credit.

Technical notes: we can provide an export tool to help migrate flags and associated metadata. SDK compatibility steps vary by language; our engineers can offer a 1-week consultation to scope the effort.

Happy to set up a call with our migration team and your engineering leads — tell me a couple of slots and we’ll coordinate.

Best,
Amy Chen
Customer Success Manager
LaunchDarkly
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 03 Aug 2027 14:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: LD renewal / consolidation quote and options

Evelyn —

Engineering position after reviewing Amy's note and our flag census:
- Migration complexity: medium. Several services depend on Optimizely experiment IDs and built-in experiment telemetry; we will need to replicate metric hooks. Expect ~3 engineer-months to port experiments + validate telemetry.
- Risk: minor customer-facing risk if experiment telemetry drifts; recommend a staged migration (pilot product -> ramp).
- Recommended mitigation: accept LD's PS credit and book 2-week engagement with their migration team to scope a pilot and reduce the unknowns.

If leadership approves the PS credit route we can start the pilot within 3 weeks of contract signature.

-Lauren
Director, Experimentation Platform Engineering
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Amy Chen <amy@launchdarkly.com>, Nate Singh <nate@optimizely.com>, Priya Desai <priya.procure@acme-corp.com>
Date: Wed, 04 Aug 2027 15:38:00 -0700
Subject: Decision & next steps — recommend consolidate to LaunchDarkly (pilot + negotiation)

Team —

Summary decision: based on cost math, engineering risk, and vendor responsiveness, I recommend we consolidate to LaunchDarkly under Scenario A (18-month commit, 28% discount + $35k PS credit). Karthik and Lauren’s engineering estimates and Amy’s commercial offer make this the lowest-risk path to capture savings in year one.

Action items:
1) Markus — please open a procurement ticket and lead commercial negotiations with Amy. Target final legal/finance sign-off by Aug 20. Attach Optimizely SOW stub (Optimizely_SOW_stub.docx) for closure/termination language review.
2) Marissa — coordinate AM outreach to Optimizely (Nate) to request a counter-proposal; keep it timeboxed to 72h.
3) Lauren & Karthik — schedule a 60-min scoping call with LaunchDarkly migration engineers (Amy to propose times). Prepare pilot checklist and telemetry parity tests.
4) Markus & Priya (Procurement) — evaluate any early termination exposure and confirm final TCO.

Attachments: FF_consolidation_cost_model.xlsx, LD_renewal_quote_2027-08.pdf, Optimizely_SOW_stub.docx

If no objections by EOD Thu (Aug 5), we’ll proceed with the procurement path above. Thanks all — this should materially simplify ops and lower unit cost for feature gating across products.

Evelyn Hart
VP, Platform & Product Operations
Redwood Inference
[Sent from mobile]
